issues.title: Missing ConfigureAwait(false) on Task.Yield
issues.description: The rule requires all await expressions in library code (non-test, non-sample projects) to use .ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid capturing the synchronization context, but the await Task.Yield() expression at line 291 omits it.
issues.rule_name: Async Methods Must Use ConfigureAwait(false) in Library Code

issues.title: Logout validation incorrectly rejects valid logout requests when HistoryEntryState is null
issues.description: The sign-out validation logic was modified to remove the null check for Navigation.HistoryEntryState before calling ValidateSignOutRequestState(). This causes ValidateSignOutRequestState() to return false when HistoryEntryState is null (since GetCachedNavigationState() returns null), which incorrectly redirects users to the logout failure page even for legitimate logout operations. The original code correctly allowed logout when HistoryEntryState is null by using the condition 'HistoryEntryState != null && !ValidateSignOutRequestState()', which only validated if state existed. This breaks backward compatibility with logout flows that don't use history state.

issues.title: Missing null check for InteractiveRequestUrl causes potential null reference in navigation
issues.description: The Redirect() method condition was changed from checking both InteractionOptions and InteractiveRequestUrl to only checking InteractionOptions. This creates a bug where if InteractionOptions is not null but InteractiveRequestUrl is null, the code will call NavigateToLogin with a null URL parameter at line 40. The NavigateToLogin method expects a non-null URL, so this will cause a null reference exception or navigation failure. The original PR properly validated both properties before choosing the navigation method.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #62755 - [Blazor] Remove obsolete APIs from Components

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes a set of [Obsolete] public APIs across the Blazor Components, Forms, Web, WebAssembly and WebAssembly.Authentication packages: Router.PreferExactMatches, AddDataAnnotationsValidation and the single-argument EnableDataAnnotationsValidation, RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions, the WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions class, WebRenderer.RendererId init, JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged, SignOutSessionStateManager, the obsolete AccessTokenResult constructor and RedirectUrl, the obsolete RemoteAuthenticationService constructor, and the internal InvokeJS extern. Each removal is recorded as *REMOVED* in PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, and the matching tests are dropped. The mechanical removals check out: I found no remaining callers of the removed symbols in src/, and the surviving EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(IServiceProvider) overload is what DataAnnotationsValidator uses.

The PR also changes behavior beyond deletion, and that part does not hold up. The sign-out flow in RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore now calls ValidateSignOutRequestState() unconditionally, so a logout with no HistoryEntryState is always rejected. The PR description says the opposite: that null state should not fail validation. The diff also adds an unexplained Task.Yield() whose comment does not match what it does, and it removes the test that covered the logout-failure redirect without adding a replacement. Separately, AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect lost its null guard on InteractiveRequestUrl, so a RequiresRedirect result with a null URL now throws instead of falling back gracefully."
structured_output.verdictRationale: The obsolete-API deletions are mechanically sound and the API baseline bookkeeping is consistent. The blocker is the sign-out behavior change. Null HistoryEntryState now fails validation, which contradicts the PR's own description and removes the fallback that legacy apps relied on, and no test covers the new path. The token-redirect null guard removal is a smaller regression that should be restored or justified.

architecture.overview:
Blazor WebAssembly authentication is driven by RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore, which handles the /authentication/logout action. Before this PR it checked two things: the interactive request state carried in NavigationManager.HistoryEntryState, and a legacy SignOutSessionStateManager that stored a flag in sessionStorage. Token acquisition returns an AccessTokenResult, and AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect() uses that result to send the user back to login.

The PR deletes the legacy sessionStorage path and the obsolete constructors and properties, and it rewires the logout guard so that only the history-state check remains. It also changes Redirect() to rely solely on InteractiveRequestUrl. The rest of the PR is API-surface cleanup in Components, Forms, Web and WebAssembly, tracked through PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt.
steps: Entry point: the logout route is handled by RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut, which reads Navigation.HistoryEntryState through GetCachedNavigationState().

Removed legacy path: SignOutSessionStateManager (sessionStorage flag) and its DI registration in WebAssemblyAuthenticationServiceCollectionExtensions are gone, along with the SignOutManager injection property.

Changed guard: ProcessLogOut now fails whenever ValidateSignOutRequestState() is false, so a null history state always results in a redirect to LogOutFailedPath. The new Task.Yield() sits before the authentication-state check.

Token redirect: AccessTokenResult drops RedirectUrl and its obsolete ctor. AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect() picks InteractionOptions when present, otherwise navigates to InteractiveRequestUrl, and it no longer checks that the URL is non-null.

Surface cleanup: Router.PreferExactMatches, the Forms AddDataAnnotationsValidation and EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(EditContext) overloads, RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions, WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions, WebRenderer.RendererId init, JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string, bool), and the RemoteAuthenticationService 4-arg ctor are removed. Each is listed as *REMOVED* in its PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt.

findings.title: Logout with null HistoryEntryState now always fails, contrary to PR description
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` (around lines 281-286) now rejects every logout when `Navigation.HistoryEntryState` is null, because it calls `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` unconditionally. The PR description says a null state should not fail validation, and only an existing-but-invalid state should. Decide the intended behavior with the maintainers. If null should pass, restore a null-state check that only fails when state exists and is invalid. If null should fail, update the PR description to say so. Either way, add a unit test in `RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs` that pins the chosen behavior for a null history state.

findings.title: Unexplained Task.Yield() added to sign-out path
findings.body:
The diff adds `await Task.Yield();` with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out". Yielding does not check authentication. It only defers the continuation to the scheduler. The next line still calls `GetAuthenticationStateAsync()` and branches on `IsAuthenticated`.

No part of the PR description mentions this, and the commit that introduced the null-state fix does not explain it. Without a stated reason, it looks like a leftover from debugging. It also changes timing on the logout path in a way nobody has described.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs" lines="288-294"}

If the yield is needed for a real ordering problem, name that problem in the comment and add a test that depends on it. If it is not needed, delete it.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` has an `await Task.Yield();` with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out" (around line 290). The yield does not verify authentication, and the PR description does not justify it. Find out whether it fixes a real ordering issue. If it does, rewrite the comment to name that issue and add a test that depends on it. If it does not, remove it.

findings.title: Null guard dropped from AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect
findings.body:
The old `Redirect()` only took the interactive branch when both `InteractionOptions` and `InteractiveRequestUrl` were non-null. The new check looks only at `InteractionOptions`, so a `RequiresRedirect` result with a null URL goes straight into `NavigateToLogin(_tokenResult.InteractiveRequestUrl, ...)` with a null string. The else branch also passes `InteractiveRequestUrl!`, which can be null for the same reason.

`AccessTokenResult` is public, and its constructor accepts `string? interactiveRequestUrl`. So a caller who builds the result themselves can hit this, and the failure is an `ArgumentNullException` thrown from inside a redirect helper.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs" lines="38-45"}

Restore the URL check in the interactive branch, or guard the else branch the same way. Failing early with a clear message is better than passing null to the navigation manager.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs`, `Redirect()` (around lines 38-45) now takes the interactive branch whenever `InteractionOptions` is non-null. It no longer checks `InteractiveRequestUrl`, and the else branch uses `InteractiveRequestUrl!`. A null URL therefore reaches `NavigateToLogin` or `NavigateTo`. Restore the null check in the interactive condition so it matches the original (`InteractionOptions != null && InteractiveRequestUrl != null`), and make sure the else branch cannot receive null. Add a test in `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/` that covers a `RequiresRedirect` result with a null URL.

findings.title: Removed logout-failure test leaves the redirect path uncovered
findings.body:
The PR deletes `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState`, which asserted the redirect to `logout-failed` and the "not initiated from within the page" history state. The PR describes this as removing tests that used obsolete APIs. But that test exercised the failure branch of `ProcessLogOut`, which the PR still has and has also changed. No replacement test was added.

After this change nothing checks that an invalid or missing sign-out state redirects to `logout-failed`. That is exactly the area where the behavior is in question (see the null-state finding above).

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs" lines="370-373"}

Rewrite the test without the legacy manager. Drive it through the history-state path with an invalid SignIn state and with a null state, and assert the navigation URI and `HistoryEntryState`.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs`, the test `AuthenticationManager_Logout_RedirectsToFailureOnInvalidSignOutState` was deleted. It covered the logout-failed redirect. Add a replacement that does not use `SignOutSessionStateManager`. Cover at least two cases: a history state that parses to a non-SignOut interaction, and a null history state. Assert the `logout-failed` URI and the "The logout was not initiated from within the page." history-state value. The expected null-state behavior must match whatever is decided for `ProcessLogOut`.

findings.title: Obsolete API removal is consistent across projects
findings.body:
The removals are applied as one unit. Every removed symbol has a `*REMOVED*` line in the matching `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, and `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` is untouched. I grepped `src/` for the removed symbols and found no callers left in production code. The only remaining `PreferExactMatches` is a parameter on a test-asset `CustomRouter`, and that does not inherit from `Router`.

The single-argument `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(EditContext)` overload has no callers either, and `DataAnnotationsValidator` and the tests use the `IServiceProvider` overload. Deleting the `[Obsolete]` `AddDataAnnotationsValidation` also removes its test along with it.

findings.title: JS interop for location changes still uses the surviving 3-argument overload
findings.body: `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged(string uri, bool isInterceptedLink)` was removed. The JS side calls `NotifyLocationChanged` through `invokeDotNetStaticMethodAsync` in `Boot.WebAssembly.Common.ts`. That call resolves to the `[JSInvokable]` 3-argument overload `(uri, state, intercepted)`, which stays in place. The `WebAssemblyHostBuilder` `DynamicDependency` uses `nameof`, which still resolves because the remaining overload carries the same name. So the browser-to-.NET path is unchanged.
